title: Images of invariant boundary components are Q-Cartier
statement:
Let $X$ be a Noetherian regular scheme [def-weil-regular-scheme], [pqf-def-locnoeth] with an admissible tame action of a finite group $G$: invariant affine opens cover $X$ and each geometric inertia has order invertible at the point. Let $B\subseteq\overline B$ be invariant strict normal crossings divisors [def-trf-strict-normal-crossings-boundary] and assume the divisorial log scheme $(X,\overline B)$ is very tame [def-trf-fs-log-blowup]. Let $q:X\to Y=X/G$ be the finite quotient. The image $D=q(B)$ is the support of an effective Q-Cartier Weil divisor: etale locally on $Y$ there is a non-zero-divisor $c$ whose zero set is exactly $D$. Here an effective Q-Cartier divisor means an effective Weil divisor some positive multiple of which is locally principal, and a Weil divisor on a normal Noetherian scheme is a finite integral combination of integral codimension-one closed subschemes. If $h:Y'\to Y$ is a birational modification with $Y'$ regular such that $(h^{-1}q(\overline B))_{\rm red}$ is a normal crossings divisor, then $(h^{-1}D)_{\rm red}$ is a union of its components and is normal crossings. It is strict normal crossings whenever the ambient divisor is strict normal crossings.

At a strict local point, write $H$ for inertia, $N=|H|$, and suppose the roots of unity of order $N$ have been adjoined. There is a local equation $b$ for $B$ which is an $H$-eigenvector and $b^N$ is invariant. Its image in the invariant local ring cuts out a Cartier divisor with support $D$.

source.place: VIII 5.3.8, printed p.125, middle paragraph, using the eigenparameter averaging of Lemma 5.3.5; VIII 5.4.1 identifies the strict local invariant quotient.
